title: Pokémon TCG rules benchmark question
description: One record per question. Questions are rewritten in our own words; no original wording is reproduced and the source is not disclosed.

id.description: q- plus a hash of the question text, so adding questions never renumbers existing ones or moves them between the public and private halves.

question_en.description: The question in English, in your own words.

question_pt.description: Optional Portuguese version. Keep the ambiguity of the original rather than tidying it up — the confusion is what makes the question hard.

category.description: tournament = how an event runs. penalty = what to do when someone breaks a rule.

answer_source.description: mechanics = three judges reading the rulebook would agree. exception = they would argue, and TPCi settled it. This split is the interesting axis: a model can reason to a mechanics answer and cannot reason to an exception.

verdict.description: open = the question is not yes/no ('what is the fix?', 'what is the result?'). Grade those on expected_points alone.

expected_points.description: Facts the answer must contain. Required when verdict is 'open', since there is no verdict to match. Graded individually, so a right answer for the wrong reason scores differently from a right one.

must_abstain.description: True when nothing in the corpus answers this. Scores whether the system refuses instead of inventing.

needs_context.description: A correct answer must ASK for these, not assume them. Penalties change with tier and division.

answer_changed_after.description: Date the correct answer last changed (a rotation, an errata, a rules update). Non-null questions are where a stale model should fail.

asked.description: Month (YYYY-MM) the question was recorded. Coarse on purpose. bench/stale.py uses it to flag rule-of-the-event keys recorded before the current handbook revision.

key_checked_against.description: Document -> ISO revision date the key was verified against (e.g. {"tcg-tournament-handbook": "2026-09-01"}). Absent means the key has not been checked against a dated document.

rule_changed.description: Present when the rule behind this key is known to have changed; says between which document revisions.

contested_reason.description: Why the question is excluded from verdict scoring: e.g. time-bound (the right answer changes with the date asked).

contested.description: Judges genuinely disagree. Scored separately, never forced to one answer.

source_ref.description: Local reference into work/*.jsonl. Never a quote.

key_checked_by.description: Name of the certified Professor or judge who verified this answer.

split.description: Assigned by hashing the id (bench/draft.py). private is never published — it is what still measures anything once the public half has entered training data.

drafted_by.description: Who wrote the question text. Separate from key_checked_by: writing a clear question and knowing the right answer are different jobs.

key_recheck.description: Present when the key was re-derived after independent runs disagreed with it. Records the problem found and the verdict it replaced, so the correction is auditable.
